channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Huang says he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board wants him
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · In his first public statement since resigning, posted on X and sent to news outlets, Huang said he had "made serious mistakes" in his personal life and was committed to cooperating with the board's independent investigation. He said employees, investors, partners and customers had called for him to come back, and that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board decides that is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, reports the board is not interested in reinstating him in any role.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: First results without Huang: revenue doubles; board chair says Huang won't return
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for August–October, up 103% from a year earlier, in its first results under interim CEO Colette Kress. Data centre sales, mostly AI chips, were $107.6 billion. Profit was $65.3 billion. Nvidia expects about $130 billion in sales next quarter, assuming no data centre chip sales to China. "Our momentum is real," Kress said. On the earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said "the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO", per Constellation Research; CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, also reports the board is against his return. Shares fell 0.44% in regular trading, then rose nearly 3% after hours, per CBS News.

item.title: AI this week: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra, for the hardest professional work such as documents, slides and coding, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a cheaper everyday model. Both are in ChatGPT and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users, and in the API. Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Sol $2 and $10. OpenAI's own charts show gains over earlier versions on most tests. Independent results are mixed, per VentureBeat: Artificial Analysis ranks Astra second overall behind Claude Fable 5.2, and some well-known developers criticised the release.

item.title: AI this week: Nvidia's sales double; board says Huang won't return
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% on a year earlier, and expects about $130 billion next quarter. It was the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. Board chair Harvey Jones said on the call that the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, per Constellation Research. Shares rose after hours.

item.title: AI model tracker: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · OpenAI's new top model, Astra, and a cheaper everyday model, Sol, in ChatGPT, Codex and the API. Astra costs $8/$40 per million input/output tokens. OpenAI reports gains on most of its tests; independent results are mixed, per VentureBeat.

item.title: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol

item.title: Anthropic: IPO price reportedly at or above the top of the range
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg News reports, citing unnamed sources, that Anthropic plans to price its shares at or above the top of its $70–78 range, with orders close to seven times the shares on offer. The Wall Street Journal reports the price could be above $80. Pricing is expected on Wednesday 18 November (US time) and trading on 19 November. These are reports; Anthropic has not announced a price.

item.title: Google Gemini: Gemini to keep 'history off' chats for about two months
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · Google will keep temporary Gemini chats, and chats made with history turned off, for about two months instead of 72 hours, TechCrunch reports. Google says the longer period helps with safety and security. It is also splitting one setting into two: one for chat history and one for whether chats are used to train AI. People who had the old setting off will have both off. The change rolls out worldwide over the coming weeks. Temporary chats are not used for training, per Google's privacy page.

item.title: US markets: Fourth straight loss for the S&P 500 as software and health shares fall
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 and the Nasdaq had its fourth loss in a row, per Reuters and CappNotes. All 11 sectors fell. Software companies such as Salesforce and Intuit, and health insurers, fell most; Reuters also points to worries about AI spending, hints from Fed officials that a rate rise is possible, and higher import prices. October retail sales rose more than forecast. Nvidia fell 0.44% before its results, then rose after hours. The opening level could not be confirmed from two reports, so this day has no gap figure.

item.title: Apple: Record share price as Apple stays the world's most valuable company
item.description: 9 Nov 2026 · After record September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, reported on 2 November, Apple's shares close at a record $350.69, valuing it at about $5.1 trillion, the most of any company in the world, per 24/7 Wall St.

item.title: Apple: First close above $5 trillion
item.description: 14 Oct 2026 · Apple ends a trading day worth more than $5 trillion for the first time. Only Nvidia had done so before, in October 2025. Apple had briefly touched $5 trillion during trading on 28 July.

item.title: Apple: Ternus's first launch: the foldable iPhone Duo
item.description: 9 Sep 2026 · At his first product event as CEO, Ternus unveils the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable phone, from $1,999. It ships on 23 October. CBS News reports new iPhone prices rose partly because of a global shortage of memory chips.

item.title: Apple: John Ternus takes over as CEO
item.description: 1 Sep 2026 · Ternus, 51, who has spent about 25 years at Apple, becomes chief executive. Cook moves to executive chairman.

item.title: Apple: Tim Cook says he will step down; John Ternus named next CEO
item.description: 20 Apr 2026 · Apple announces that Cook, CEO for 15 years, will hand over to hardware engineering chief John Ternus on 1 September and become executive chairman. AP reports Apple's market value rose by more than $3.6 trillion under Cook, from $350 billion in August 2011 to about $4 trillion.

item.title: Apple: Apple turns 50
item.description: 1 Apr 2026 · Apple marks 50 years since its founding with a letter from Tim Cook titled '50 Years of Thinking Different' and events in its stores.

item.title: Apple: Apple touches $4 trillion
item.description: 28 Oct 2025 · Strong demand for the iPhone 17 pushes Apple's market value above $4 trillion for the first time during trading, making it the third company to get there after Nvidia and Microsoft. It closed just below, at about $3.99 trillion.

item.title: Apple: Vision Pro headset, then Apple Intelligence
item.description: Feb 2024 · Apple releases the Vision Pro mixed-reality headset at about $3,500. In June it announces Apple Intelligence, its AI features. Both get mixed reviews, and Apple is widely viewed as trailing rivals in AI, Invezz reports.

item.title: Apple: Briefly worth $3 trillion, a first for any company
item.description: 3 Jan 2022 · Apple's shares touch $182.88, making it the first company ever valued at $3 trillion, though only briefly during the day.

item.title: Apple: Macs move to Apple's own chips
item.description: Nov 2020 · The first Macs with Apple-designed M1 chips arrive, after Apple announced in June that it would stop using Intel's chips.

item.title: Apple: Apple becomes the first $1 trillion US company
item.description: 2 Aug 2018 · Apple becomes the first publicly traded US company valued at $1 trillion. It passes $2 trillion on 19 August 2020.

item.title: Apple: Apple Watch opens a new product category
item.description: 24 Apr 2015 · The Apple Watch goes on sale. Sales start slowly but grow once Apple focuses it on fitness and health.

item.title: Apple: Steve Jobs dies at 56
item.description: 5 Oct 2011 · Jobs dies in Palo Alto, California, after a long fight with pancreatic cancer, six weeks after stepping down.

item.title: Apple: Jobs steps down; Tim Cook becomes CEO
item.description: 24 Aug 2011 · Jobs resigns as chief executive and recommends chief operating officer Tim Cook as his successor. The board names Cook CEO and Jobs chairman.

item.title: Apple: The iPad
item.description: 27 Jan 2010 · Apple announces the iPad tablet, which runs the same apps as the iPhone on a bigger screen. It goes on sale in the US on 3 April 2010.

item.title: Apple: The App Store opens with 500 apps
item.description: 10 Jul 2008 · Apple lets outside developers sell apps for the iPhone. The App Store opens with 500 apps, a day before the iPhone 3G goes on sale.

item.title: Apple: Jobs unveils the iPhone, and 'Computer' is dropped from Apple's name
item.description: 9 Jan 2007 · Jobs introduces the iPhone, a touchscreen phone, iPod and internet device in one, priced at $499 and $599 in the US. Apple Computer also renames itself Apple Inc. The iPhone goes on sale on 29 June 2007.

item.title: Apple: Macs switch to Intel chips
item.description: Jun 2005 · Apple announces it will move the Mac from PowerPC chips to Intel's, citing speed and energy use. The first Intel Macs arrive in January 2006.

item.title: Apple: The iTunes Music Store sells songs for 99 cents
item.description: 28 Apr 2003 · Apple opens an online store selling single songs for 99 cents each with no subscription, at first only to US customers on Macs.

item.title: Apple: The iPod: '1,000 songs in your pocket'
item.description: 23 Oct 2001 · Apple unveils the iPod, a $399 music player that stores up to 1,000 songs and syncs with the iTunes software on a Mac. It marks Apple's move beyond computers.

item.title: Apple: Mac OS X replaces the old Mac software
item.description: 24 Mar 2001 · Apple releases Mac OS X, built on NeXT's technology. It becomes the foundation for the software that runs Macs, iPhones and iPads today.

item.title: Apple: The iMac starts the comeback
item.description: 6 May 1998 · Jobs unveils the iMac, a colourful all-in-one computer built for getting online. It goes on sale on 15 August 1998 and becomes the best-selling Mac of all time; Apple returns to profit that year.

item.title: Apple: Jobs becomes interim CEO
item.description: 16 Sep 1997 · Twelve years after he was forced out, Jobs is named Apple's interim chief executive. He cuts most of the product line to focus on a handful of computers.

item.title: Apple: Microsoft invests $150 million in Apple
item.description: 6 Aug 1997 · On stage at Macworld in Boston, Jobs announces a deal with long-time rival Microsoft. It buys $150 million of Apple shares and commits to making Office for the Mac for five years. Some of the crowd boos when Bill Gates appears on the big screen. Apple's shares rose 33% that day.

item.title: Apple: The board pushes out Gil Amelio
item.description: 9 Jul 1997 · With Apple losing money and its shares at a 12-year low, the board removes Amelio as chief executive. Jobs takes on a bigger role with the board and management.

item.title: Apple: Apple buys NeXT, and Jobs comes back
item.description: 20 Dec 1996 · Struggling to build a modern operating system of its own, Apple agrees to buy NeXT for $400 million. Jobs returns as an adviser to chief executive Gil Amelio, who had taken over earlier in 1996. NeXT's software later becomes the basis of Mac OS X.

item.title: Apple: The Newton stumbles and Sculley is replaced
item.description: 2 Aug 1993 · Apple's first handheld computer, the Newton MessagePad, has a troubled launch. It contributes to Sculley being replaced as chief executive by Michael Spindler in 1993.

item.title: Apple: The PowerBook sets the shape of the modern laptop
item.description: 21 Oct 1991 · Apple's PowerBook pushes the keyboard back towards the screen, leaving room for palm rests and a pointing device in front. Most laptops still follow this layout.

item.title: Apple: Steve Jobs is pushed out of Apple
item.description: 17 Sep 1985 · After the Mac sells poorly, Sculley strips Jobs of his duties in April and defeats his attempt to take back control in May. Jobs resigns in September and starts a new computer company, NeXT. Wozniak had already left in February 1985.

item.title: Apple: The Macintosh, launched with the '1984' ad
item.description: 24 Jan 1984 · Jobs unveils the Macintosh, which brings the mouse and on-screen windows to more people at about a quarter of the Lisa's price. It is launched with a TV ad called '1984'.

item.title: Apple: The Lisa flops, and Apple hires a boss from Pepsi
item.description: Jan 1983 · Apple launches the Lisa, one of the first personal computers with a mouse and on-screen windows. At $9,995 it fails to sell. In 1983 Apple also recruits PepsiCo president John Sculley as chief executive, partly to mentor the young Jobs.
